documents.s: Claudeforce: Salesforce in Claude (Sept 2026 open beta)

documents.t: Claudeforce is a four-strand partnership, not a product. Only one strand — Salesforce in Claude — is opening in September 2026. Conflating the strands is how RevOps teams end up scoping the wrong pilot. Guided walkthrough1 of 4 1Strand 1 — Salesforce in Claude (Sept 2026 open beta)⌄ A Salesforce plugin that runs INSIDE the Claude app. Sellers stay in Claude; Claude reaches into their org via Salesforce's Hosted MCP. This is the strand this page is about. ←PreviousNext→ 2Strand 2 — Claude inside Salesforce products⌄ The reverse direction: Anthropic's models available as first-class citizens across Agentforce (Atlas Reasoning Engine, Agentforce Vibes, Agentforce Coworker, Agent Builder). Different UX, different admin surface, different rollout schedule. ←PreviousNext→ 3Strand 3 — Claude as the default model in Slack⌄ Slack AI features (huddles summaries, channel recaps, message drafting) start using Claude as the default backing model. Governed differently — see the Slack auth route below. ←PreviousNext→ 4Strand 4 — Commercial cross-adoption⌄ Salesforce becomes a large Anthropic customer; Anthropic becomes a large Salesforce customer. Interesting for procurement, irrelevant for the technical setup. ←PreviousNext→ The rest of this page is strand 1: Salesforce in Claude.

The single non-obvious thing about Claudeforce is that the plugin does not register a tool per capability. Salesforce's Headless 360 Hosted MCP Server (Beta, July 2026) exposes exactly four MCP tools, and Claude reaches every skill by composing them. Guided walkthrough1 of 4 1Discover⌄ Semantic search across a vector index of every API and skill in the connected org. Claude passes its interpretation of your request; Discover returns a ranked list of candidate operations. This is the reason 'find me the deal-health thing for this account' doesn't require 200 pre-registered tools cluttering context. ←PreviousNext→ 2Describe⌄ For a chosen candidate, Describe returns the technical contract: parameters, dependencies, ordered steps, side effects. Claude uses it to verify Discover surfaced the right thing before it commits to running anything. ←PreviousNext→ 3Dispatch⌄ Runs the chosen operation. Routes to the right endpoint. Enforces user access guards before the call reaches Salesforce. This is the write path — validation rules, Flows, Apex triggers, and CPU governor limits all fire as normal downstream of Dispatch. ←PreviousNext→ 4Dispatch Read-Only⌄ GET-only variant. Same discovery flow, same access checks, but the tool physically cannot mutate. This is the pilot-safe default and the tool the read-only skills bind to. ←PreviousNext→ Two implications most launch posts miss: The tool surface stays small and stable, but the catalog of skills grows independently on Salesforce's side — Claude doesn't need a new tool registration to reach a new skill. Field-level security, object permissions, and sharing rules apply to every tool call — enforcement happens in the org, not in Claude. If a user can't see a field in the Salesforce UI, Discover won't surface it and Dispatch would deny it anyway.
documents.s: The 4-tool architecture that scales to 37 skills

documents.t: Claudeforce ships with two OAuth models stapled to the same-looking plugin, and they have very different security postures. Getting this wrong is how you accidentally give every rep in the org the effective permissions of one integration user. Guided walkthrough1 of 2 1Route A — Salesforce in Claude (per-user OAuth)⌄ Uses Salesforce External Client Apps with the mcp_api scope. A single admin does the one-time org-level connect; each seller then authorizes as themselves. Every Claude tool call runs as the requesting individual, with THEIR profile, permission sets, sharing rules and field-level security. This is the correct posture for anything user-visible. ←PreviousNext→ 2Route B — Claude in Slack (client credentials)⌄ Uses OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow with a dedicated integration user. Access bundles share ONE agent credential across users. Every request runs as the same integration user — meaning that user's permissions become the effective ceiling for everyone touching it. Convenient, but the wrong shape for anything with per-user data isolation requirements. ←PreviousNext→ Watch out If you provision the Slack integration user with a wide sales-ops profile so 'it just works,' every Slack user routed through it inherits that effective access. Restrict the integration user's profile to the narrowest scope Slack actually needs, then add capability with permission sets — same principle as any shared service account.
documents.s: The two auth routes — and why the difference matters

documents.t: Salesforce named only a handful of skills at launch; more will drop through late 2026. What you can plan for right now is that every skill lands in one of three authority levels, and the interface makes them look identical. It's on you to classify. Named skill (Aug 2026) Authority level Rough Dispatch route Daily briefing Read-only Dispatch RO Pipeline review Read-only Dispatch RO Forecast narrative Read-only Dispatch RO Meeting preparation Read-only Dispatch RO Deal-health review Read-only Dispatch RO Win/loss analysis Read-only Dispatch RO Salesforce hygiene Recommend Dispatch RO → drafts Activity logging Write Dispatch (POST/PATCH) The remaining ~29 skills are unpublished at launch; the same triage applies as they land: Guided walkthrough1 of 3 1Read-only (Dispatch RO only)⌄ Analyzes, summarizes, retrieves. Cannot mutate. Enable freely for the pilot cohort. Failure mode is 'wrong answer,' not 'wrong write.' ←PreviousNext→ 2Recommend (Dispatch RO + drafts)⌄ Analyzes AND proposes changes, but leaves the actual mutation as a draft for a human. Enable after the read-only tier is behaving. Failure mode is a bad draft that a seller might approve without reading — measure correction rate, not just speed. ←PreviousNext→ 3Write (Dispatch POST/PATCH/DELETE)⌄ Directly mutates CRM data. Every write goes through the org's validation rules, Flows, Apex triggers, and CPU governor limits, EXACTLY as if a human clicked Save. Enable last, per-skill, with per-user profile scoping, and only after you've measured recommend-tier accuracy for at least 4 weeks. ←PreviousNext→
documents.s: The 37 skills, classified by authority level

documents.t: Guided walkthrough1 of 6 11. Audit the profiles you're about to expose⌄ Any over-provisioned profile that was harmless behind a slow UI becomes genuinely risky behind a fast agent. Before piloting, run a permissions audit on the users you'll invite: which objects, which fields, which record-type sharing. The plugin will faithfully enforce whatever those profiles say — including whatever historical over-provisioning nobody noticed. ←PreviousNext→ 22. Bind pilot users to a locked-down permission set⌄ Create a Claudeforce Pilot permission set: specific objects, specific fields, read-only to start. Assign it in addition to their normal profile so you can remove it cleanly at the end of the pilot without touching baseline access. ←PreviousNext→ 33. Start with Dispatch Read-Only everywhere⌄ Enable only read-only skills for the first two sprints. This lets you measure accuracy without a rollback surface. Watch for hallucinated field names or wrong record lookups — those are the failure modes that survive into the write tier. ←PreviousNext→ 44. Pick THREE workflows across the three authority levels for the write-tier pilot⌄ One read-only, one recommend, one write. Different risk profiles surface different governance gaps, and one pilot per tier is cheaper than one pilot per skill. ←PreviousNext→ 55. Version your API baseline⌄ Salesforce in Claude requires API v67.0+; Winter '27 introduces v68.0. If your org auto-upgrades to Winter '27 during the beta window (Sept–Oct 2026), lock the plugin's API version explicitly so a platform upgrade doesn't shift semantics on you mid-pilot. ←PreviousNext→ 66. Ban team-owned MCP connections during the beta⌄ If individual teams stand up their own Hosted MCP Servers to 'move faster,' you've reinvented shadow IT with cleaner packaging. Centralize MCP governance under the same admins who own connected apps and profiles. ←PreviousNext→ Seller prompt template: safe Monday pipeline briefing (read-only tier) CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ You are preparing my Monday pipeline briefing from Salesforce. Every Monday at 07:00 local: 1. Use the "Pipeline review" skill on my named accounts (owner = me, stage != Closed Lost, close date in current quarter). 2. Use the "Deal-health review" skill on the top 10 by amount. 3. Use the "Meeting preparation" skill for accounts I have a meeting with in the next 5 business days. Constraints (do NOT violate): - Read-only pass only. If any skill proposes a write (update stage, log activity, change amount) STOP and surface it as a draft in the output — do NOT dispatch it. - Do not log activities on my behalf. Do not update fields. - If a skill returns a field you cannot see under my profile, do not guess the value — flag it as "hidden by permissions". Produce a single briefing: - 3-bullet TL;DR - "Pipeline movement since last Monday" (opportunity-level, cite the Salesforce record IDs) - "Deals I should touch this week" (with why, from deal-health) - "Meetings this week" (with prep pack from meeting-preparation) - "Proposed writes (NOT DISPATCHED)" — every draft change the agent wanted to make, so I can review in one place. Two things this prompt does that most 'copy this template' posts don't: It pins the pilot to read-only with an explicit "if the skill proposes a write, STOP" invariant. In a scheduled or long-running Claude session you can't answer a follow-up 'are you sure?' — invariants have to live in the prompt. It asks the model to surface every write it wanted to make in one place, so you can measure the recommend-tier accuracy of a skill before you promote it to write-tier. This is the cheapest way to earn the promotion.
documents.s: Setting up a pilot — the RevOps checklist

documents.t: Guided walkthrough1 of 4 11. Over-provisioned profiles become live blast radius⌄ The same permission set that was mostly-fine behind a UI is genuinely dangerous behind an agent that can Dispatch 30 writes/minute. Fix: profile audit BEFORE pilot, not after. ←PreviousNext→ 22. Automation side effects fire on every Dispatch write⌄ Dispatch PATCH is a normal Salesforce write. Every validation rule, Flow, Process Builder, Apex trigger, and CPU-time governor limit fires just like a human click. A well-meaning skill running in a loop can trip CPU limits or fan out unwanted Flow-driven emails. Fix: instrument your automation on the pilot org before turning on write-tier skills. ←PreviousNext→ 33. Winter '27 lands during open beta⌄ Winter '27 production upgrades (Sept–Oct 2026) collide with the Claudeforce open beta. If a skill breaks in the middle of the window, you'll be debugging TWO simultaneous platform changes. Fix: pin API version on the plugin, and schedule the pilot cohort's Winter '27 upgrade OUTSIDE the beta window if you can. ←PreviousNext→ 44. Slack route ≠ Claude route⌄ Because Slack uses client-credentials with an integration user, giving 'Slack access to Claudeforce' is not the same governance shape as giving individual users the plugin in Claude. Treat them as two separate rollouts with two separate audit trails. ←PreviousNext→
documents.s: The four traps that will bite you

documents.t: Salesforce has been shipping Agentforce since 2024 and Claude has been ONE of its foundation models since late 2025. Claudeforce doesn't replace Agentforce — it adds a new surface (the Claude app) and formalizes Claude across four Agentforce layers (Atlas Reasoning Engine, Agentforce Vibes, Agentforce Coworker, Agent Builder). Model optionality stays: Agent Builder still offers Amazon Nova alongside Claude. Rough decision table for teams staring at both: You want to... Reach for Give sellers a chat interface that reasons over live CRM Salesforce in Claude (the plugin) Embed AI features INTO your Salesforce UI (records, list views, buttons) Agentforce Build a custom agent with tools, memory, escalation policies Agent Builder (inside Salesforce) Automate repeatable back-office CRM work end-to-end Agentforce Coworker Use Claude to write Salesforce code (Apex, LWC) Agentforce Vibes If more than one row applies, the wrong choice is to pick one and force it — Claudeforce is designed so the plugin, Agentforce, and Agent Builder are complementary, and users can move between them within the same org.
documents.s: Where Claudeforce sits relative to Agentforce

documents.t: You need a machine-to-machine integration. The plugin is a human-in-the-loop chat surface. For unattended CRM writes at scale, wire the Headless 360 MCP Server into Managed Agents directly, without the Claude app in the middle. You already ship an Agentforce experience your sellers know. Adding a second surface fragments your training and doubles governance work. Pick the one your team lives in. You have zero Salesforce admins to govern this. The plugin makes the org more powerful and more reachable — that's a bad combo without someone owning profiles, permission sets, and MCP connections. Your compliance posture forbids inference over customer data. Even though the plugin routes inference through Amazon Bedrock inside the Salesforce Trust Boundary, prompt content and returned data still leave the storage layer. Read your DPA before piloting.
documents.s: When NOT to use Salesforce in Claude

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें मध्यम आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-06-20। कौन से कनेक्टर मौजूद हैं, और प्लान के अनुसार उपलब्धता, अक्सर बदलती रहती है — मौजूदा विकल्पों की पुष्टि ऐप/हेल्प सेंटर में करें। इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. कनेक्टर Claude ऐप्स को चैट के बाहर — आपके टूल्स और डेटा (ड्राइव, इश्यू ट्रैकर, कैलेंडर, डेटाबेस, और बहुत कुछ) — तक पहुँचने देते हैं, ताकि Claude वास्तविक सिस्टम से जवाब दे सके और उन पर कार्रवाई कर सके। पर्दे के पीछे ये ओपन Model Context Protocol (MCP) द्वारा संचालित होते हैं।

कनेक्टर के बिना, Claude केवल वही जानता है जो बातचीत में है। एक कनेक्टर के साथ, यह (आपकी अनुमति से) किसी कनेक्टेड सेवा से प्रासंगिक जानकारी निकाल सकता है — जैसे कोई डॉक्युमेंट ढूँढना, हाल के इश्यू पढ़ना, एक कैलेंडर जाँचना — और उसे अपने जवाब में उपयोग कर सकता है।
कनेक्टर MCP का ऐप-सामने वाला रूप हैं। ठीक यही प्रोटोकॉल Claude Code में MCP और API पर को संचालित करता है। अवधारणा एक बार सीखें; यह सभी सतहों पर लागू होती है।

सेवा को कनेक्ट करें (जहाँ समर्थित हो वहाँ OAuth के ज़रिए अधिकृत करें)। न्यूनतम विशेषाधिकार दें — केवल वही पहुँच जो कार्य को चाहिए। स्वाभाविक रूप से पूछें — "मेरा Q3 प्लानिंग डॉक ढूँढो और जोखिमों का सारांश दो।"

एक कनेक्टर पहुँच + (कभी-कभी) कार्रवाइयाँ है केवल उन्हीं सेवाओं और स्कोप को अधिकृत करें जिन पर आप भरोसा करते हैं। बाहरी स्रोतों से निकाली गई सामग्री प्रॉम्प्ट इंजेक्शन ले जा सकती है — जब कोई कनेक्टर अविश्वसनीय सामग्री पढ़ता है तो सतर्क रहें। किसी थर्ड-पार्टी कनेक्टर को सक्षम करने से पहले समीक्षा करें कि वह क्या कर सकता है (थर्ड-पार्टी कोड की समीक्षा)।
Claude Code में MCP सर्वर MCP और टूल्स से कनेक्ट करना (API) आपके मौजूदा टूल्स में AI यह पेज साझा करें X LinkedIn Reddit Hacker News लिंक कॉपी करें

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें मध्यम आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-08-05। Cowork on web + mobile launched July 7, 2026 (Max first, other paid plans rolling in weeks after). Availability, quota, and exact connector coverage are moving fast — confirm against the official blog post and the Schedule recurring tasks in Claude Cowork help-center article before you rely on a number here. Update (September 16, 2026): Cowork and chat merged into one Claude. Scheduled tasks, connectors, skills and files all carried over and work as described below — but you no longer open a separate Cowork surface to reach them. इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. Cowork stopped being a desktop-only workspace on July 7, 2026. It now runs on web (claude.ai), iOS and Android, and — the part most write-ups bury — sessions execute on Anthropic's servers, not your machine. That single architectural change is what unlocks the headline feature: scheduled tasks that run with your laptop closed, your phone in your pocket, and no device online at all. This page is the practical field guide: what actually works on which surface, how to set a scheduled task up correctly the first time, and the small handful of gotchas you only notice after your 6 AM Monday briefing silently fails because it needed a local file. What you'll learn Understand why moving Cowork execution off your device changes the product (scheduled runs, cross-device handoff, mobile approval prompts) — and where the tradeoffs land Pick the right surface (desktop / web / mobile) for a given job, using the capability matrix Set up a scheduled Cowork task correctly on the first try, with the right approval mode, frequency and working folder Design a mobile approval flow that doesn't silently stall when you're asleep or on a plane Avoid the four gotchas that break scheduled runs in production: local-only tools, Fable-5-on-desktop-only, Dispatch vs Remote, and connector auth drift
documents.s: Cowork Scheduled Tasks: Agents That Run With No Device On

documents.t: Before July 2026, a Cowork session was a process inside the Claude Desktop app on your Mac or PC. Close the laptop, session dies. Kill the app, session dies. This is why the pre-July Cowork loop always started with "open desktop, keep it awake." The July launch introduces remote sessions: the Cowork loop lives in Anthropic's cloud, your session state and files persist against your Claude account, and any surface (web, mobile, desktop) is just a viewer + input device for the same underlying session. Two direct consequences: Scheduled tasks are possible. A recurring task can wake up at 06:00 Monday, do 45 minutes of work, and drop a draft in your account — with zero devices online, because there's no device in the loop. Cross-device handoff is free. Start a task at your desk, close the laptop, and see the same session mid-run on your phone. There's nothing to sync — the session was never on your laptop. The tradeoff is the capability matrix below: anything that needs to touch your local machine (files on disk, your browser, your OS) can only run on desktop, because that's the only surface with a foot in both worlds.
documents.s: The one shift that matters: sessions moved to Anthropic's servers

documents.t: Capability Desktop app Web (claude.ai) Mobile (iOS/Android) Cowork sessions (interactive) ✓ ✓ (beta) ✓ (beta) Scheduled Cowork tasks ✓ (create + monitor) ✓ (create + monitor) ✓ (monitor + approve) Local file access ✓ ✗ ✗ Browser use (local browser automation) ✓ ✗ ✗ Computer use (OS control) ✓ ✗ ✗ Live artifacts (in-session preview) ✓ ✗ ✗ Connected tools (Gmail, Slack, GDrive, Calendar, web) ✓ ✓ ✓ Installed Skills ✓ ✓ ✓ Plugins ✓ ✓ ✓ Mobile push for approval prompts (via linked phone) (via linked phone) ✓ (native) Fable 5 model in Cowork ✓ (latest Desktop only) see gotchas see gotchas The rule of thumb If the task only needs connected tools + Skills + web (email triage, "read these three docs and draft me an update", weekly report from Google Sheets), it runs anywhere — schedule it. If it needs your files, your browser, or your machine, it stays desktop-and-live only.

The three modes get conflated. They're different beasts: Guided walkthrough1 of 3 1Interactive Cowork session⌄ You start it, you're watching, Claude works over a long horizon on your active goal. Lives on Anthropic's servers now, so you can hand it off between devices. Best for: multi-hour work you want to steer as it happens. ←PreviousNext→ 2Scheduled Cowork task⌄ You define a prompt + a cadence (hourly / daily / weekdays / weekly / manual). Each run spawns a fresh Cowork session with the tools, skills and plugins you specified. Runs remotely, on schedule, whether or not any device is online. Best for: recurring prep work — Monday 06:00 briefings, hourly inbox triage, end-of-day rollups. ←PreviousNext→ 3Dispatch (desktop-only)⌄ Legacy shape: fire off a background task from an active desktop session that keeps running while you continue chatting. Requires the desktop app to stay awake because the process still lives locally. Best for: local-machine work you want to background while you keep collaborating. Do NOT confuse it with a scheduled remote task — Dispatch dies when the app closes. ←PreviousNext→ The mental shortcut: Dispatch = local background, Scheduled Task = cloud on a cadence, Interactive = you're at the wheel.
documents.s: Interactive Cowork vs a Scheduled Task vs Dispatch

documents.t: A scheduled task needs six things — five settings and one prompt. Get any of the settings wrong and the run will look "successful" but do the wrong thing. Guided walkthrough1 of 6 1Task name⌄ Short, human. This is what you'll see in the scheduled-tasks list and in mobile notifications. 'Monday client prep' beats 'briefing-v2'. ←PreviousNext→ 2Prompt / instructions⌄ Write it as if talking to a colleague who joins fresh every run — because every run IS a fresh session. State the goal, the sources (which connectors, which skills, which folders), the output shape you want, and any invariants (e.g. 'never send email, always leave as draft'). ←PreviousNext→ 3Frequency⌄ Pick one of hourly / daily / weekdays / weekly / manual. There is no cron syntax and no sub-hourly options — if you need 'every 5 min', you're on the wrong tool (use the API + your own scheduler). ←PreviousNext→ 4Approval mode⌄ The critical setting. Options are auto-approve (Claude proceeds without asking, good for read-only tasks), ask-on-mobile (Claude pauses at a decision point and pings your phone — safe default for anything that writes), or hold-for-review (task always ends with a draft you review later). ←PreviousNext→ 5Model (optional)⌄ Defaults to the Cowork default for your plan. Pick a smaller/cheaper model for heavy read-summarize loops; pick top-tier only when reasoning quality actually moves the outcome. ←PreviousNext→ 6Working folder (optional)⌄ Scopes the session's file writes to a specific project/folder in your Claude account. Skip it and outputs land in a default location — which is fine for one task, a mess when you have twelve. ←PreviousNext→ Scheduled task prompt template: Monday 06:00 client briefing CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ You are preparing my Monday morning brief for the Acme account. Every Monday at 06:00 local: 1. Read the last 7 days of email in the "Acme" Gmail label. Group by thread; note anything that expects a reply from me. 2. Pull calendar events with "Acme" in the title or attendees from the coming week. Note prep needed for each. 3. Search the web for news about Acme (company name + "acquisition", "layoffs", "product launch") in the last 7 days. Cite sources. 4. Read the Google Doc "Acme - Running Notes" for open questions. Produce a single briefing doc titled "Acme brief — <this-monday-date>" in the "Client briefings" project folder. Structure: - 3-bullet TL;DR at the top - "Needs a reply from me" list (with links) - "This week" list (calendar + prep) - "News since last brief" (with sources) - "Open questions" (from the running-notes doc) DO NOT send any email. Leave a follow-up email as a DRAFT in Gmail titled "Acme weekly check-in" pre-filled with the TL;DR — I'll edit and send. Two things to notice about this prompt: The invariant ("DO NOT send any email... leave as DRAFT") is spelled out. In a scheduled run you cannot ask a follow-up "are you sure?" — the invariants have to be in the prompt. The output location + naming is precise. When these run weekly for months, you want them findable, not scattered under default titles.
documents.s: Setting up a scheduled task, the right way

documents.t: ask-on-mobile sounds friendly until it fires at 03:00 and the run silently stalls waiting for you. Two rules make this reliable: Guided walkthrough1 of 2 1Match approval mode to blast radius⌄ Read-only or draft-only actions → auto-approve. Anything that sends, publishes, deletes, or spends money → ask-on-mobile with a fallback in the prompt: 'if I haven't responded within 30 minutes, save as draft and end the task'. The prompt-level fallback matters because the platform will not time you out for you. ←PreviousNext→ 2Make the notification title tell you what's about to happen⌄ In the prompt, wrap decision points in a specific ask: 'Before sending anything, request approval with the exact subject line and first 200 chars of the body.' Push notifications truncate — front-load the important bits so you can approve/deny from the lock screen without opening the app. ←PreviousNext→ Watch out Push approvals block the task until you answer. If you never answer, the run sits — it doesn't automatically fall through to a safe default. Bake a 'if no response, do X' timeout into the prompt itself, or use hold-for-review instead.
documents.s: Mobile approval flow — designing for "I'm asleep"

documents.t: Guided walkthrough1 of 4 11. Local-only tools quietly disable the run⌄ If the prompt asks the task to 'open my downloads folder', 'automate my browser', or 'take a screenshot of my screen', the remote session has no way to do that. The run won't crash — it'll just skip or improvise. Fix: audit your scheduled prompts and swap local-machine actions for connected-tool equivalents (Google Drive instead of local files, web fetch instead of local browser, etc). ←PreviousNext→ 22. Fable 5 in Cowork still needs the latest Desktop⌄ As of the July 2026 launch, running the Fable 5 model inside a Cowork session requires the latest Claude Desktop app. If you schedule a task that pins Fable 5 and rely on it running remotely, verify current support — this constraint is expected to relax but check before pinning. ←PreviousNext→ 33. Dispatch is NOT a scheduled task⌄ Backgrounded Dispatch work from an active desktop session dies when you close the app. If you actually need 'run this weekly, no matter what', don't Dispatch — create a scheduled task. ←PreviousNext→ 44. Connector auth drift kills silent runs⌄ OAuth tokens to Gmail, Slack, Google Drive can expire, get revoked, or hit permission changes. A scheduled task under an expired connector produces empty output and no obvious error. Fix: for anything that runs weekly or less often, add a first-step self-check in the prompt ('confirm you can read the Acme Gmail label; if not, produce a one-line error at the top of the doc and stop'). ←PreviousNext→
documents.s: The four gotchas that break scheduled Cowork runs

documents.t: Scheduled Cowork tasks are a product feature — great for personal / small-team recurring work you want visible in your Claude account, with human approval in the loop. They're the wrong tool when you need: Sub-hourly cadence — the smallest scheduled-task interval is hourly. Programmatic orchestration — dozens of parallel runs, dynamic scheduling, or tight integration with your infra. Reach for Managed Agents, or roll your own with the Agent SDK + a cron/queue you already run. Server-side memory across runs — Cowork tasks pass state via files in your account, which is fine for docs but coarse for structured state. For structured cross-run memory, use Managed Agents Memory Stores. Deep multi-agent coordination — for many-agents-collaborating, see Cowork & Agent Teams and Native Multi-Agent APIs.

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-06-20। Claude ऐप्स में कस्टम निर्देशों और स्टाइल के सटीक नाम और स्थान बदलते रहते हैं — ऐप/हेल्प सेंटर में पुष्टि करें। इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. हर चैट में "संक्षिप्त रहो" या "मैं एक नर्स हूँ, उसके अनुसार समझाओ" दोहराते-दोहराते थक गए? कस्टम निर्देश और स्टाइल आपको अपनी डिफ़ॉल्ट सेटिंग्स एक बार सेट करने और उन्हें हर जगह लागू करने देते हैं।

स्थायी तथ्य और प्राथमिकताएँ सेट करें — आप कौन हैं, आप क्या करते हैं, आपको जवाब कैसे पसंद हैं — और Claude उन्हें सभी बातचीतों में लागू करता है। यह सिस्टम प्रॉम्प्ट का कंज़्यूमर-ऐप संस्करण है (और डेवलपर्स के लिए CLAUDE.md का चचेरा भाई)। शामिल करने लायक अच्छी चीज़ें: आपके बारे में संदर्भ ("मैं एक छोटी बेकरी चलाता हूँ"; "मैं Python में कोड करता हूँ")। आउटपुट प्राथमिकताएँ ("डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से छोटे बुलेट जवाब दो"; "हमेशा अपना तर्क दिखाओ")। सख्त नियम ("कभी emoji का उपयोग मत करो"; "मेट्रिक इकाइयाँ")।

documents.t: स्टाइल टोन/फ़ॉर्मेट बदलते हैं (संक्षिप्त, औपचारिक, व्याख्यात्मक, आदि) और प्रति-बातचीत बदले जा सकते हैं। किसी स्टाइल का उपयोग तब करें जब आप इस चैट के लिए एक अलग आवाज़ चाहते हों, अपने स्थायी निर्देशों को फिर से लिखे बिना।

जब कोई टकराव होता है तो अधिक विशिष्ट/बाद वाला संदर्भ जीतता है — इसलिए किसी प्रोजेक्ट के निर्देश या आपके संदेश में एक स्पष्ट माँग आपकी ग्लोबल डिफ़ॉल्ट सेटिंग्स को ओवरराइड कर सकती है। आश्चर्य से बचने के लिए इन्हें सुसंगत रखें।
documents.s: वे कैसे एक-दूसरे पर लागू होते हैं

documents.t: निर्देशों को छोटा और सच्चा रखें — CLAUDE.md की तरह, फ़ालतू भरमार और पुराने नियम नुकसान पहुँचाते हैं। कस्टम निर्देशों में राज़ न डालें। जैसे-जैसे आपकी ज़रूरतें बदलती हैं, उन्हें कभी-कभी दोबारा देखें।

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-10-20। Announced October 8, 2026. Claude Dashboards is in beta on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise; Claude Motion is in beta on Team and Enterprise only. On the same day Docs, Slides and Design left beta and became available on every plan, including Free — on Enterprise they turned on by default on October 15, 2026. Both betas are off by default on Enterprise until an owner enables them. Availability and connector lists move quickly — confirm in the Help Center before you build on anything here. इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. Two new templates landed in the artifact panel on October 8, 2026, and they are not variations on the ones already there. Claude Dashboards reaches outside the conversation into your data warehouse. Claude Motion produces something the other templates cannot: a moving image — and it produces it as code, not as video. The same announcement quietly ended the beta on Docs, Slides and Design, which are now on every plan including Free. If you read an AILmanac page (or anyone else's guide) written before October 8 saying those three are "paid, beta," that sentence is now wrong. What you'll learn Tell Dashboards and Motion apart from the templates you already have, and from a plain artifact Know exactly which plan gets which, and what an Enterprise owner has to switch on Understand the one mechanism behind each: a SQL query per chart, and an animation compiled from editable code Avoid the sharing trap — who sees what when you share a dashboard, and why a connector-backed artifact can never have a public link Recognize the three jobs these are the wrong tool for Act on the December 14, 2026 Claude Design deadline before it passes

Template What it produces Plans Status Docs A living, multi-tab document All, incl. Free GA Slides A presentable deck All, incl. Free GA Design Visuals, mockups, prototypes All, incl. Free GA Dashboards Charts driven by live queries against your data Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise Beta Motion A short animation, exported as MP4 Team, Enterprise Beta On Enterprise, both new templates are off until an owner turns them on in organization settings, under Artifacts — and an owner can narrow access to specific groups with custom roles. On Team, Motion is on by default.
documents.s: The five templates, at a glance

documents.t: You ask a question in plain language; Claude writes a SQL query for each chart and runs it against your data source. That is the whole product, and understanding it explains every strength and every limit that follows. Supported data warehouses: Amazon Redshift, BigQuery, ClickHouse, Databricks and Snowflake. It can also read apps you have already connected to Claude, Salesforce being the headline one.

Because each chart is backed by a named query rather than a model's recollection, a dashboard is auditable in a way a chat answer is not. Every chart shows its own query and when its data was last refreshed. That turns the usual trust problem inside out: instead of asking "did Claude hallucinate this number," you click the chart and read the SQL that produced it. This is the single habit worth forming on day one. Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1Ask for the decision, not the chart⌄ "Build a dashboard of this quarter's pipeline by region" gets you a chart. "I need to decide where to move two reps next quarter — show me what would tell me that" gets you a chart plus the comparison that makes it actionable. Anthropic's own guidance is to say what you want to know, not just what to plot. ←PreviousNext→ 2Name the tables or the app⌄ Say where the data lives. Pointing at a specific warehouse table or connected app is the difference between one query and three guesses. ←PreviousNext→ 3Open every chart's query before you trust the number⌄ This is the step people skip. Read the SQL: check the date range, the filter, the join, and whether it counts rows or sums a column. A correct-looking number from the wrong filter is the actual failure mode here, not invention. ←PreviousNext→ 4Refine conversationally⌄ "Add a filter for region," "split new versus renewal," "use fiscal quarters." Claude rewrites the query rather than redrawing a static picture. ←PreviousNext→ 5Hand off when it gets deep⌄ Anthropic's framing is explicit: dashboards are made for quick, exploratory questions. When a question needs real analysis, send the dashboard onward to a tool built for it. ←PreviousNext→ A dashboard brief that produces something you can act on CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ Build me a dashboard from our Snowflake warehouse (schema: SALES_PROD). The decision I'm making: which two regions get the next headcount. Show me: 1. Closed-won revenue by region, last 4 fiscal quarters, as a trend 2. Win rate by region over the same period 3. Average deal cycle in days by region 4. Open pipeline by region, split new business vs renewal Rules: - Use fiscal quarters, not calendar. - Exclude deals marked is_test = true. - For every chart, label the exact table you queried. - If a field I named doesn't exist, say so and ask — do not substitute a similar-sounding column. That last rule earns its place. The nastiest dashboard error is not a broken chart — it is a plausible chart built on amount when you meant amount_arr.

A dashboard is a starting point, not a home. Anthropic lists onward destinations including Amplitude, Grafana, Hex, Mixpanel, Omni, Perplexity, PostHog and Sigma, with Databricks Genie, Looker, monday.com and Tableau named as coming. Read that list as a statement of intent: Dashboards is positioned as the fastest way to ask a question, and explicitly not as a replacement for the BI tool where your governed metrics live.

Dashboards start private to you. Sharing one makes it an artifact that calls a connector, and connector-backed artifacts follow rules that surprise nearly everybody: Watch out Queries run as the viewer, not as you. Per Anthropic: "When someone opens your artifact, it connects to their connectors and data sources." Two colleagues can open the same dashboard and legitimately see different numbers. A viewer without access sees an error, not your data: "If they don't have access to an underlying data source, that part of the artifact shows an error instead of your data." That is the feature working correctly — it is also why your dashboard looks broken to the person you sent it to. There is no public link. "There are no external or public links and no per-person recipient selection. Anyone in your organization who has the link can open the artifact." Live data and no-login external access are mutually exclusive on the same page. Connecting apps to an artifact is a web-and-desktop capability on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise. Don't plan a mobile-first review loop around it. The practical consequence: a dashboard is an internal instrument, not a client deliverable. If an outside recipient needs the numbers, export the figures into a Doc, a deck, or a generated file and send that.
documents.s: The sharing model — read this before you share anything

documents.t: This is the fact that most coverage gets wrong, so it is worth stating plainly: Motion does not generate video. Claude writes editable code that animates text, numbers, shapes, images and charts, and the artifact plays like a short video. The direct consequence, in Anthropic's words, is that it cannot create realistic footage or people. That restriction is also the whole advantage. Because the animation is a program: You can change one word, one number or one timing value and everything else stays exactly as it was. The same brief, re-rendered after a data correction, is still the same animation — not a new roll of the dice. You can direct it in prose ("slow down the second scene") or edit it directly in the editor. If that mechanism sounds familiar, it is the same idea as the broader code-driven explainer-video pipeline — Motion is the first-party, no-setup version of it.

Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1Choose it over a deck only when motion carries meaning⌄ A sequence, a process, a value changing over time, a walkthrough of steps. If the content is a list, make Slides instead — animating a list is slower to produce and slower to read. ←PreviousNext→ 2State audience, venue and length up front⌄ "30 seconds, for an all-hands, playing on a big screen behind me" and "90 seconds, for new-customer onboarding email" produce legitimately different animations. Attach the source report or data instead of retyping it. ←PreviousNext→ 3Create it from chat, or pick the template⌄ Ask in any conversation, choose Output then Motion in the message box, or start from a Motion template in the Artifacts tab. Pick explicitly when Claude keeps producing a deck. ←PreviousNext→ 4Iterate on one thing at a time⌄ "Slow down the second scene," "make the revenue figure land after the chart finishes drawing." Single changes land reliably; a list of five rarely does. ←PreviousNext→ 5Export as MP4 and finish elsewhere if needed⌄ Anthropic names Adobe, Descript, HeyGen, Higgsfield, invideo, Luma AI and Runway as tools you can open the output in, with Canva and Captions listed as coming. Voiceover, captions and music are not documented as Motion features — plan to add them downstream. ←PreviousNext→ Brief an animation that doesn't need a second attempt CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ Turn the attached Q3 report into a 30-second animated explainer. Audience: the whole company at an all-hands, on a projector behind a speaker. It plays once, with no narration from the file itself. Structure, four scenes: 1. The one number that matters (revenue, with last quarter for contrast) 2. Where the growth came from — animate the regional chart drawing in 3. The one thing that got worse, stated plainly 4. What we're doing about it next quarter, three short lines Constraints: - Readable from the back of a room: large type, high contrast, no more than seven words on screen at once. - No decorative motion. Every movement should mean something changed. - Use only figures from the attached report. If a number I asked for isn't in it, leave the slot empty and tell me.

An honest reference says what a feature is bad at. Three cases: You want… Don't use Use instead A governed metric your whole company reports on Dashboards — it answers questions, it does not define metrics Your BI layer; send the dashboard there A live data page a client opens without logging in Dashboards — connector-backed artifacts have no public link Export the figures into a Doc or deck, or a generated file Footage, a presenter, a talking head Motion — there is no video model behind it A video tool; Motion's MP4 can be a component inside it And one cost note that applies to both: there is no separate price. Dashboards and Motion count toward your plan's usage limits like anything else, and Anthropic flags that longer or more complex animations use more of your allowance. The plans and billing page has the general shape.
documents.s: When these are the wrong tool

documents.t: The October 8 changes came with a sunset. The standalone Claude Design site closes on December 14, 2026, after which claude.ai/design simply takes you to Claude. If your team ever used it, this is a real to-do with a date on it: Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1Migrate design systems from the Artifacts page⌄ Open Artifacts in Claude and click "Migrate team design systems," from the banner or the Claude Design menu. Each migrated design system keeps its owner and the people it was shared with. Anyone who can use Claude Design can start the migration — it is not owner-only. ←PreviousNext→ 2Know what will not come across⌄ Empty design systems and ones built from a built-in starter theme are not migrated. Neither are your chats with Claude, nor comments on projects and design systems — those stay in the standalone version and are deleted when it closes. ←PreviousNext→ 3Save anything you need out of chats and comments⌄ This is the irreversible part. Public links to projects in the standalone version also stop working after it closes. ←PreviousNext→ 4Check one visibility side effect⌄ A published, non-private design system becomes visible organization-wide after migrating. Review which ones that applies to before you click. ←PreviousNext→ 5Enterprise: confirm the toggles first⌄ Artifacts must be enabled, and on Enterprise design systems are off by default until an administrator turns them on. Do that before the migration, not after. ←PreviousNext→

documents.t: Check yourself 0/4 Key takeaways October 8, 2026: Dashboards and Motion arrived in beta; Docs, Slides and Design left beta and reached every plan including Free. Any guide still calling those three 'paid, beta' is out of date. Dashboards writes a SQL query per chart. Open the query before you trust the number — the real failure mode is a correct-looking figure from the wrong filter or column. Shared dashboards run as the viewer. Different people see different data, and a viewer without access sees an error — by design. No connector-backed artifact can have a public link. A dashboard is an internal instrument; for external recipients, export. Motion is code, not video: endlessly editable and perfectly repeatable, but it can never produce footage or people. No voiceover or captions documented — add those downstream. Anthropic scopes Dashboards to quick, exploratory questions and names onward destinations like Grafana, Hex and Sigma. Treat it as the fastest way to ask, not as your BI layer. Calendar item: the standalone Claude Design site closes December 14, 2026. Migrate design systems from the Artifacts page, and save chats and comments first — those are deleted.

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-06-20। Claude कौन सी फ़ाइल प्रकार बना सकता है और कैसे, यह प्लान/सतह के अनुसार भिन्न होता है और बदलता रहता है — ऐप/हेल्प सेंटर में पुष्टि करें। इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. स्क्रीन पर टेक्स्ट से परे, Claude असली, डाउनलोड करने योग्य फ़ाइलें तैयार कर सकता है — Word डॉक्युमेंट, PowerPoint डेक, Excel स्प्रेडशीट, PDF — फ़ॉर्मेट किए गए और उपयोग के लिए तैयार। बढ़िया जब आपको केवल एक जवाब नहीं, बल्कि एक डिलीवरेबल चाहिए हो।

Word (.docx) — रिपोर्ट, पत्र, प्रस्ताव, फ़ॉर्मेट किए गए डॉक्युमेंट। PowerPoint (.pptx) — किसी रूपरेखा या नोट्स से स्लाइड डेक। Excel (.xlsx) — डेटा, फ़ॉर्मूले, सरल मॉडल के साथ स्प्रेडशीट। PDF — उपरोक्त के प्रिंट-तैयार संस्करण।

डिलीवरेबल का वर्णन करें: प्रकार, दर्शक, लंबाई, खंड, टोन। सामग्री या स्रोत प्रदान करें (नोट्स, डेटा, एक रूपरेखा) — या Claude से पहले उसका ड्राफ़्ट बनाने के लिए कहें। फ़ाइल के लिए कहें ("इसे .docx के रूप में एक्सपोर्ट करो"), फिर दोहराएँ ("एक टाइटल पेज जोड़ो," "टेबल को चार्ट बनाओ," "स्लाइड 3 को कसो")। Turn these notes into a 6-slide investor update deck (.pptx): traction, revenue, roadmap, team, ask. Clean and minimal. Notes: {paste}

संरचना दें। आपके अनुरोध में हेडिंग/खंड → साफ़-सुथरा आउटपुट। स्प्रेडशीट के लिए असली डेटा प्रदान करें — और किसी भी गणना की गई संख्या की पुष्टि करें (हैल्युसिनेशन); ऐसे आँकड़े न भेजें जिन्हें आपने जाँचा नहीं है। एक्सपोर्ट करने से पहले परिष्कृत करें — अंतिम फ़ाइल में सुधारने की बजाय चैट में सुधारना आसान है। ये क्षमताएँ पर्दे के पीछे स्किल्स द्वारा संचालित होती हैं — वही विचार जिसे आप स्वयं भी लिख सकते हैं।
आर्टिफ़ैक्ट्स: लाइव, चलने योग्य आउटपुट लेखन और सामग्री निर्माण व्यवसाय, मार्केटिंग और रणनीति यह पेज साझा करें X LinkedIn Reddit Hacker News लिंक कॉपी करें

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-06-20। प्लान के नाम और सीमाएँ बदलती रहती हैं — मौजूदा विवरण के लिए प्लान, सीमाएँ और बिलिंग और आधिकारिक प्राइसिंग पेज देखें। इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. claude.ai Claude का उपयोग करने का सबसे आसान तरीका है — कोई इंस्टॉल नहीं, कोई कोड नहीं। पहली ही बैठक में इससे मूल्य कैसे प्राप्त करें, यहाँ बताया गया है।

claude.ai पर एक अकाउंट बनाएँ। फ्री टियर बुनियादी बातें सीखने के लिए पर्याप्त है; पेड टियर उपयोग की सीमाएँ बढ़ाते हैं और अधिक सुविधाएँ अनलॉक करते हैं। आपको अभी निर्णय लेने की ज़रूरत नहीं है — जब आप तैयार हों तो प्लान, सीमाएँ और बिलिंग देखें।
documents.s: साइन इन करें और एक प्लान चुनें

documents.t: नीचे एक मैसेज बॉक्स — यहाँ टाइप करें या पेस्ट करें। ऊपर बातचीत — आपकी और Claude की बारी, क्रम में। पिछली चैट्स का एक साइडबार — हर चैट का अपना संदर्भ होता है। अटैचमेंट — फ़ाइलें, इमेज, या PDF डालें और उनके बारे में पूछें। यह मोबाइल पर और वॉइस द्वारा भी उपलब्ध है।

"सर्च" न करें — किसी समझदार सहकर्मी से जैसे पूछते हैं वैसे पूछें, संदर्भ और एक स्पष्ट माँग के साथ: "मैं अक्टूबर में रोम की 3-दिन की यात्रा की योजना बना रहा हूँ, दो लोगों के लिए जिन्हें खाना और इतिहास पसंद है, मध्यम बजट पर। हर दिन एक ज़रूर-करने लायक चीज़ और पास के एक लंच स्थान के साथ एक दिन-प्रतिदिन की रूपरेखा तैयार करें।" फिर सरल भाषा में परिष्कृत करें: "दिन 2 को कुछ कम पर्यटक-भरे विकल्प से बदलें," "अनुमानित लागत जोड़ें," "इसे एक चेकलिस्ट बनाएँ।" यही आगे-पीछे का संवाद वह जगह है जहाँ जादू होता है — देखें प्रॉम्प्टिंग की मूल बातें।

संदर्भ दें। लक्ष्य, दर्शक, फ़ॉर्मेट, टोन। (यह आपके मन को नहीं पढ़ सकता।) दोहराएँ। पहला जवाब एक ड्राफ़्ट होता है। जो महत्वपूर्ण हो उसकी पुष्टि करें। तथ्य, संख्याएँ और उद्धरण आत्मविश्वास के साथ गलत हो सकते हैं — देखें हैल्युसिनेशन।

प्रोजेक्ट्स — अपनी खुद की फ़ाइलों और निर्देशों वाला एक वर्कस्पेस। कस्टम निर्देश और स्टाइल — अपनी डिफ़ॉल्ट सेटिंग्स एक बार सेट करें। आर्टिफ़ैक्ट्स — एक साइड पैनल में लाइव डॉक्युमेंट और चलने योग्य ऐप्स पाएँ।
आपके पहले 5 मिनट Claude से बात करना (वॉइस मोड) रोज़मर्रा की उत्पादकता यह पेज साझा करें X LinkedIn Reddit Hacker News लिंक कॉपी करें

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-06-20। क्रॉस-चैट मेमोरी का व्यवहार और उपलब्धता प्लान के अनुसार भिन्न होती है और बदलती रहती है — मौजूदा विवरण की पुष्टि ऐप/हेल्प सेंटर में करें। इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से हर बातचीत एक कोरी स्लेट होती है। मेमोरी सुविधाएँ Claude को आपके बारे में उपयोगी तथ्य चैट्स के बीच ले जाने देती हैं — ताकि आपको हर बार अपना परिचय दोबारा न देना पड़े।

लोग कुछ अलग-अलग चीज़ों को "मेमोरी" कहते हैं — उन्हें भ्रमित न करें: प्रकार यह क्या है कॉन्टेक्स्ट विंडो एक चैट के भीतर काम करने वाली मेमोरी (इसके समाप्त होने पर भुला दी जाती है) — देखें टोकन और कॉन्टेक्स्ट क्रॉस-चैट मेमोरी Claude आपके बारे में तथ्य बातचीतों के बीच याद रखता है (इस पेज का विषय) कस्टम निर्देश स्थायी तथ्य जिन्हें आप स्पष्ट रूप से सेट करते हैं प्रोजेक्ट्स किसी वर्कस्पेस तक सीमित ज्ञान

जब सक्षम हो, तो Claude आपकी प्राथमिकताओं, चल रहे प्रोजेक्ट्स, या आपके साझा किए गए विवरणों जैसी चीज़ें याद रख सकता है — जिससे यह हर सेशन में अजनबी की बजाय एक निरंतर असिस्टेंट जैसा महसूस होता है। उपलब्धता और नियंत्रण आपके प्लान पर निर्भर करते हैं।
documents.s: क्रॉस-चैट मेमोरी कैसे मदद करती है

documents.t: जो याद रखा गया है उसकी समीक्षा और संपादन करें (जहाँ ऐप नियंत्रण प्रदान करता है)। यदि आप एक कोरी स्लेट या अधिक गोपनीयता चाहते हैं तो इसे क्लियर या निष्क्रिय करें। महत्वपूर्ण तथ्यों की सटीकता के लिए इस पर निर्भर न रहें — स्मरण पर भरोसा करने की बजाय महत्वपूर्ण विवरणों की पुष्टि करें। गोपनीयता का ध्यान रखें — मेमोरी जानकारी को बनाए रखती है; ऐसा संवेदनशील डेटा स्टोर न करें जिसे आप रखा हुआ नहीं चाहते। देखें गोपनीयता। स्पष्ट, अंतर्निहित से बेहतर है ऐसे तथ्यों के लिए जो अवश्य लागू होने चाहिए (आपकी भूमिका, इकाइयाँ, सख्त नियम), कस्टम निर्देश सेट करें या एक प्रोजेक्ट का उपयोग करें — यह मेमोरी के उन्हें याद रखने की आशा करने से अधिक विश्वसनीय है।
टोकन, कॉन्टेक्स्ट और मेमोरी कस्टम निर्देश और स्टाइल गोपनीयता और डेटा हैंडलिंग यह पेज साझा करें X LinkedIn Reddit Hacker News लिंक कॉपी करें

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-06-20। मोबाइल सुविधाएँ और प्लेटफ़ॉर्म उपलब्धता बदलती रहती है — मौजूदा क्षमताओं की पुष्टि ऐप स्टोर / आधिकारिक डॉक्युमेंट में करें। इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. Claude केवल एक डेस्कटॉप टैब नहीं है। iOS और Android ऐप्स इसे आपकी जेब में रखते हैं — विचारों को पकड़ने, त्वरित सवालों, और चलते-फिरते वॉइस के लिए आदर्श।

चलते-फिरते पकड़ें। लिफ़्ट में आया एक विचार, एक व्हाइटबोर्ड की फ़ोटो, एक त्वरित "इसका सारांश दो" — मोबाइल उस इनपुट के लिए चमकता है जिसे आप अन्यथा खो देते। वॉइस-फ़र्स्ट। फ़ोन पर टाइप करने की बजाय बोलना अक्सर तेज़ होता है — देखें वॉइस मोड। फ़ोटो और स्क्रीनशॉट। एक मेन्यू, एक फ़ॉर्म, एक एरर मैसेज, एक संकेत की तस्वीर लें, और उसके बारे में पूछें (मल्टीमॉडल इनपुट)। निरंतरता। बातचीत और प्रोजेक्ट्स सिंक होते हैं, इसलिए आप मोबाइल पर शुरू कर सकते हैं और डेस्कटॉप पर समाप्त कर सकते हैं।
दीर्घ-रूप लेखन और संपादन। बड़े डॉक्युमेंट या ढेर सारी फ़ाइलों के साथ काम करना। आर्टिफ़ैक्ट्स और कोई भी ऐसी चीज़ जहाँ स्क्रीन की जगह मदद करती है। डेवलपर काम (Claude Code डेस्कटॉप/CLI है)।

वॉइस से पकड़ें → स्क्रीन पर परिष्कृत करें। चलते हुए वॉइस से एक अव्यवस्थित विचार ब्रेन-डंप करें, फिर बाद में Claude से कहें "उस ट्रांसक्रिप्ट को एक साफ़ रूपरेखा में बदलो।" फ़ोन कच्चा माल इकट्ठा करता है; आप कहीं भी पॉलिश करते हैं। शेयर शीट का उपयोग करें मोबाइल पर आप अक्सर अन्य ऐप्स से टेक्स्ट/लिंक/इमेज सीधे Claude में शेयर कर सकते हैं — कॉपी-पेस्ट के बिना "इसका सारांश दो" पूछने का एक तेज़ तरीका।
Claude से बात करना (वॉइस मोड) Claude.ai के साथ शुरुआत रोज़मर्रा की उत्पादकता यह पेज साझा करें X LinkedIn Reddit Hacker News लिंक कॉपी करें

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-10-20। Announced September 16, 2026. The merged experience rolled out gradually, starting with Pro and Max on web, desktop and mobile, then Team and Free; Enterprise organizations got at least 30 days' notice. Update — October 8, 2026: Claude Docs, Claude Slides and Claude Design left beta and are available on every plan, including Free, on by default (on Enterprise they turned on by default on October 15, 2026). Two further templates, Dashboards and Motion, arrived in beta the same day — see Dashboards & Motion. Check the Help Center article for current status before relying on anything here. इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. On September 16, 2026, Anthropic collapsed three products into one. Chat, Cowork (the agentic workspace) and Claude Design stopped being separate places you had to choose between. There is now one conversation box, and Claude decides what the task needs. The official framing is short: "Ask Claude for what you need, and it can decide which tool to use." The practical consequence is longer, and it is what this page is about — because a merge like this moves settings, retires habits, and ships two new document tools whose limits are not obvious until you hit them. What you'll learn Understand what actually merged on September 16, 2026 — and why 'no mode to choose' changes how you open a task Find every setting that moved: global instructions, web search, research, and file storage Pick correctly between Claude Docs, Claude Slides, Claude Design, a plain artifact, and a downloaded .docx/.pptx Use Claude Docs the way it's designed: tabs, inline comments, @Claude edits, and real-time co-authoring Know the eight limits that will bite you — no version history, no comment-only role, charts that don't refresh, and the compliance configurations where Docs is simply unavailable Predict the usage-limit cost of agentic work now that everything runs in one conversation
documents.s: One Claude: The Merge, Claude Docs & Claude Slides

documents.t: Nothing you had is thrown away. Per Anthropic: "Existing Cowork tasks, projects, connectors, skills, artifacts, and files carry over, and those Cowork tasks open as they did before, so you can continue them." What changes is the entry point. Previously you decided the shape of the work before you described it — chat for a question, Cowork for a project. Now you describe the work and Claude picks the machinery, with the same context, skills and connectors available from any conversation.

This is the part that generates the most "where did my button go" confusion, and it is the part no third-party write-up covers. Four things relocated: What you used Where it is now Global instructions Settings → General Web search toggle Gone — it's automatic. Claude decides when to search Research Type /deep-research, or use the + button Your files Settings → Storage folder Watch out The web-search toggle is not hidden, it is removed. If your workflow depended on forcing search off for a private or offline-reasoning task, that lever no longer exists in the UI — say it in the prompt instead ('answer from the conversation only; do not search the web').

The merge shipped Claude Docs and Claude Slides as new tools, and moved Claude Design inside conversations. All three are templates — a starting shape for an artifact, not a separate app. Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1Claude Docs — living documents⌄ Rich-text documents saved to your Claude account, with headings, tables and other formatting, and more than one tab (like sections of a notebook). You and Claude and your colleagues all write in the same document, at the same time. Exports to Word (.docx), PDF, Markdown (.md) and Google Docs. Reach for it when the document itself is the deliverable and it will keep changing. ←PreviousNext→ 2Claude Slides — presentations⌄ Decks built from your notes, a report, or the work already in the conversation. You can edit any slide directly, present without leaving Claude, and export to PowerPoint and PDF. Reach for it when you need a deck out of material you already produced. ←PreviousNext→ 3Claude Design — visuals and prototypes⌄ Visuals, mockups, prototypes, one-pagers and landing pages, built against your design system. Exports as a .zip, PDF, PowerPoint, or standalone HTML. Reach for it when the output is visual or needs to match a brand. ←PreviousNext→ 4A plain artifact — code, apps, charts⌄ Still there, unchanged, on every plan including Free. A runnable mini-app, a chart, a diagram, a script. Reach for it when the thing needs to execute rather than be read. See Artifacts. ←PreviousNext→ 5A generated file — .docx / .pptx / .xlsx / .pdf⌄ A one-shot file Claude builds and you download. No live editing surface, no sharing, no comments. Reach for it when you need a file to hand off and never touch inside Claude again. See Generating Real Files. ←PreviousNext→ The distinction that matters most is the last two: a Claude Doc is a living document with a URL, collaborators and comments; a generated .docx is a download. If you asked for "a Word doc" pre-merge and got a file, asking the same way now may get you a Doc you then export — which is usually what you wanted, but it is a different object with different sharing rules.
documents.s: The three templates: which one do you actually want?

documents.t: Guided walkthrough1 of 3 1Ask in any conversation⌄ Plain language is enough — 'turn the plan we just worked through into a product spec I can share with the team.' Claude asks a few questions before it starts, then drafts the doc on screen. ←PreviousNext→ 2Choose a template explicitly⌄ Select Output in the message box and choose a template. Use this when Claude keeps picking a different shape than you want. ←PreviousNext→ 3Start from the Artifacts tab⌄ Pick a template from the gallery, then brief Claude. Useful when the document, not the conversation, is the thing you came for. ←PreviousNext→ Brief a Claude Doc so the first draft is close CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ Create a Claude Doc: a one-page product spec for the export feature we just designed. Structure it in four tabs: 1. Summary — problem, proposed solution, who it's for 2. Requirements — numbered, testable, each with a rationale 3. Open questions — things I still need to decide, with your recommendation and the tradeoff for each 4. Rejected alternatives — what we considered and why not Rules: - Pull the decisions from this conversation. Do not invent requirements I did not state. - Where I was vague, leave a comment asking me the question instead of guessing. - Add a table comparing the three export formats we discussed. Ask me anything you need before you start drafting.

Three editing paths coexist, which is the point of the tool: You type. Click into the doc and type. Changes save automatically. You ask. Request a change conversationally; Claude edits and explains what it did and why. You comment. Select text and leave a comment for your collaborators — and mention @Claude in a comment to have Claude make that edit in place. Claude replies in the thread, makes the change, and explains it. Claude also leaves its own comments while drafting, to explain a choice or ask you a question. This is the behavior worth designing your prompt around: telling Claude to ask in a comment rather than guess (as in the prompt card above) converts silent hallucination risk into a visible question you can answer. You can also ask Claude to add a chart, diagram, graph or timeline to a doc.

People with edit access work on the same doc at the same time as you and Claude, and everyone's edits appear in real time. Viewer Editor Read ✅ ✅ Edit ❌ ✅ Comment ❌ ✅ Export ❌ ✅ Sharing rules differ sharply by plan: Pro / Max — share with anyone who has the link. Team / Enterprise — invite specific people or a group, or share with everyone in your organization. Docs cannot be shared outside your organization, by link or by email invitation. Either way — opening a shared doc requires a Claude account, and only the owner can rename or delete a doc.
Docs work on web, desktop, Claude Code, and mobile — but the iOS and Android apps are view-only: no editing and no template selection from a phone. Plan around that if your review loop is mobile.

Every one of these is documented, and every one surprises somebody in week one. Guided walkthrough1 of 9 1No version history yet⌄ There is no way to see or restore an earlier state of a doc. Anyone with edit access can overwrite anything, and your only recovery is an export you took earlier. For a document that matters, export to Markdown at each milestone until history ships. ←PreviousNext→ 2No comment-only access level⌄ The roles are viewer and editor, nothing between. A reviewer who should comment but not edit does not exist as a permission — grant edit and rely on trust, or grant view and collect feedback elsewhere. ←PreviousNext→ 3Charts and diagrams don't update automatically⌄ A chart Claude added is a snapshot. Change the underlying numbers in the doc and the chart keeps showing the old ones until you ask Claude to regenerate it. Treat every visual as stale until re-asked. ←PreviousNext→ 4Team and Enterprise cannot share externally⌄ No link sharing, no email invitation outside the organization. If you need to send a doc to a client, export it (Word, PDF, Markdown, Google Docs) and send the export. ←PreviousNext→ 5Mobile is view-only⌄ iOS and Android can read a doc. They cannot edit one or pick a template. ←PreviousNext→ 6Unavailable under CMEK, ZDR and HIPAA⌄ Claude Docs is not available for organizations configured with customer-managed encryption keys, zero data retention, or HIPAA. This is the single most important fact for regulated teams, and it is not a rollout delay — it is an exclusion. ←PreviousNext→ 7Not in the Compliance API yet⌄ Activity inside a doc is not recorded in the Compliance API. If your audit posture depends on that export, doc activity is currently a blind spot. ←PreviousNext→ 8The standalone Claude Design site closes December 14, 2026⌄ If your team used the standalone site, migrate design systems from the Artifacts page before then — chats, comments and public project links from the standalone version are deleted when it closes. Full checklist on Dashboards & Motion. ←PreviousNext→ 9The newer templates still have the Enterprise toggle⌄ Docs, Slides and Design are now on by default everywhere, including Enterprise as of October 15, 2026. The two beta templates are not: Dashboards and Motion are off on Enterprise until an owner turns each one on in organization settings, under Artifacts. ←PreviousNext→
documents.s: The limits that will bite you

documents.t: The unified experience does not yet support GitHub integration ("Add from GitHub"), conversation branching, search across older Cowork tasks, Dispatch (existing users only), or incognito chats for file and code creation. If your workflow leans on branching or on searching your Cowork history, that capability is temporarily gone — not moved.
documents.s: Also not supported yet in the merged experience

documents.t: There is no separate price. The relevant sentence is about usage limits: "Everything you do with Claude counts toward your plan's usage limits. Longer agentic tasks that search the web, run code, or create files generally use more than a quick question." Claude Docs counts the same way. The merge makes this sharper than it sounds. Previously, opening Cowork was a deliberate act — you knew you were starting expensive work. Now a casually-phrased request in the same box can trigger a long agentic run that searches, executes code and writes files. The cost signal moved from the door to the prompt. If you are on a plan where limits matter, say what you want explicitly: Keep a request cheap when you only want an answer CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ Answer from this conversation only. Do not search the web, do not run code, and do not create any files or artifacts. Two paragraphs. And the inverse, when you do want the full machinery: Ask for the expensive version on purpose CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ Take this as a full task, not a chat answer. Research the three vendors below, check their current pricing pages, build a comparison spreadsheet, and turn the recommendation into a Claude Doc I can share with the team. Cite every figure with a link and the date you read it. Vendors: [A], [B], [C]

Guided walkthrough1 of 5 1Re-home your global instructions⌄ They moved to Settings → General. Open them once and re-read them: instructions written for chat-only Claude ('you cannot browse the web', 'ask before doing anything long') can now actively fight the merged behavior. ←PreviousNext→ 2Stop reaching for the web-search toggle⌄ It's gone. Put search intent in the prompt — either 'check current sources' or 'do not search'. ←PreviousNext→ 3Relearn research⌄ Type /deep-research or use the + button. It is a command now, not a mode. ←PreviousNext→ 4Audit anything that assumed Cowork was separate⌄ Scheduled tasks, connectors and skills carried over, but prompts that said 'this is a Cowork task' as a signal to work harder no longer signal anything. Replace that framing with explicit scope, as in the prompt cards above. ←PreviousNext→ 5Decide your Docs export cadence⌄ Until version history ships, pick a milestone rhythm — export to Markdown whenever the doc reaches a state you would be upset to lose. ←PreviousNext→

Check yourself 0/4 Key takeaways One conversation, no mode to choose: the cost signal moved from the door (opening Cowork) to the prompt. Say explicitly when you want a cheap answer and when you want the full agentic run. Four things moved: global instructions → Settings → General; web search → automatic, steer in the prompt; research → /deep-research or +; files → Settings → Storage folder. A Claude Doc is a living document with collaborators and comments; a generated .docx is a download. Choose deliberately — they share rules differ completely. Design your prompt around Claude's comments: tell it to ask in a comment rather than guess, and you convert invention into a visible question. Two limits deserve a workaround today: no version history (export to Markdown at milestones) and charts that never refresh (regenerate after every data change). Regulated teams: Claude Docs is unavailable under CMEK, ZDR and HIPAA, and doc activity is not in the Compliance API yet.

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-06-20। प्लान के नाम, कीमतें और सीमाएँ नियमित रूप से बदलती रहती हैं — मौजूदा संख्याओं के लिए हमेशा आधिकारिक प्राइसिंग पेज जाँचें। हम जानबूझकर यहाँ डॉलर की राशि नहीं बताते। इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. आपको कौन सा Claude प्लान चाहिए? यहाँ इसके बारे में कैसे सोचें — ऐसी कीमतें बताए बिना जो अगले महीने पुरानी हो जाएँगी (उनके लिए आधिकारिक प्राइसिंग जाँचें)।

टियर मोटे तौर पर किसके लिए Free Claude आज़माना, हल्का व्यक्तिगत उपयोग Pro नियमित व्यक्तिगत उपयोग — अधिक उपयोग, अधिक क्षमता Max भारी व्यक्तिगत उपयोगकर्ता जो Pro सीमाओं तक पहुँच जाते हैं Team छोटी टीमें — साझा वर्कस्पेस और प्रबंधन Enterprise वे संगठन जिन्हें एडमिन, सुरक्षा, स्केल और नियंत्रण चाहिए (सटीक नाम/संरचना बदल सकती है — प्राइसिंग पेज पर पुष्टि करें।)

कंज़्यूमर प्लान सीमित करते हैं कि आप एक विंडो में कितना उपयोग कर सकते हैं (मैसेज/उपयोग जो समय के साथ रीसेट होते हैं), और उच्च टियर उन सीमाओं को बढ़ाते हैं। जब आप किसी सीमा तक पहुँचते हैं तो आमतौर पर आपसे इसके रीसेट होने तक प्रतीक्षा करने या अपग्रेड करने के लिए कहा जाता है — आपका काम खोता नहीं है, आप बस रुक जाते हैं। भारी मॉडल (और लंबी बातचीतें) आपके आवंटन को तेज़ी से खर्च करते हैं। यदि आप सीमाओं तक पहुँच रहे हैं, तो एक त्वरित उपाय है नए विषयों के लिए ताज़ा चैट शुरू करना और प्रॉम्प्ट को केंद्रित रखना (वही विचार जो कॉन्टेक्स्ट प्रबंधन में है)।

Free से शुरू करें। सीखें कि आप वास्तव में इसका उपयोग किसके लिए करते हैं। जब सीमाएँ वास्तविक काम में बाधा डालें तो Pro में अपग्रेड करें। यदि आप एक पावर यूज़र हैं और फिर भी सीमाओं तक पहुँच रहे हैं तो Max पर जाएँ। Team/Enterprise जब सहकर्मियों को साझा पहुँच, एडमिन, या अनुपालन की ज़रूरत हो।
ऐप प्लान = उपयोग सीमाओं के साथ एक फ़्लैट सब्सक्रिप्शन (यह पेज)। API बिलिंग = आप जो बनाते हैं उसके लिए प्रति टोकन भुगतान। अलग मॉडल, अलग पेज।

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-06-20। प्रोजेक्ट सुविधाएँ और सीमाएँ प्लान के अनुसार भिन्न होती हैं और बदलती रहती हैं — मौजूदा व्यवहार की पुष्टि ऐप/हेल्प सेंटर में करें। इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. एक प्रोजेक्ट Claude.ai में एक समर्पित वर्कस्पेस है जो अपनी खुद की फ़ाइलें, ज्ञान और निर्देश बंडल करता है। हर चैट में वही डॉक्युमेंट दोबारा अपलोड करने और संदर्भ दोबारा समझाने की बजाय, आप इसे एक बार सेट करते हैं — और प्रोजेक्ट में हर बातचीत पहले से जानकार होकर शुरू होती है।

आधारित जवाब। अपने डॉक्युमेंट जोड़ें (एक हैंडबुक, स्पेसिफ़िकेशन, नोट्स) और Claude उनसे जवाब देता है — RAG का एक अंतर्निहित, नो-कोड स्वरूप। स्थायी संदर्भ। प्रोजेक्ट निर्देश इसके अंदर हर चीज़ के लिए एक स्कोप किए गए सिस्टम प्रॉम्प्ट की तरह काम करते हैं। व्यवस्थित। एक विषय/क्लाइंट/पहल के बारे में सभी चैट्स एक साथ रहती हैं।

एक प्रोजेक्ट बनाएँ और इसे एक स्पष्ट उद्देश्य दें। ज्ञान जोड़ें — वे फ़ाइलें/टेक्स्ट जो इसे हमेशा जाननी चाहिए। प्रोजेक्ट निर्देश लिखें — भूमिका, परंपराएँ, क्या करना है/किससे बचना है। चैट करना शुरू करें — हर बातचीत ज्ञान + निर्देश विरासत में पाती है।

एक क्लाइंट/अकाउंट वर्कस्पेस (उनके डॉक्युमेंट + आपके नोट्स)। Q&A के लिए एक कोडबेस या प्रोडक्ट नॉलेज बेस। आपकी स्टाइल गाइड और पिछले लेखों के साथ एक लेखन प्रोजेक्ट (ताकि ड्राफ़्ट आपकी आवाज़ से मेल खाएँ)। किसी कोर्स के लिए अध्ययन, सिलेबस और सामग्री लोड की गई।

ज्ञान को सावधानी से चुनें — प्रासंगिक, मौजूदा फ़ाइलें सब कुछ डंप करने से बेहतर हैं (शोर रिट्रीवल को नुकसान पहुँचाता है)। निर्देशों को कसा हुआ और सच्चा रखें (वही नियम जो कस्टम निर्देशों का है)। ऐसा संवेदनशील डेटा न जोड़ें जिसे स्टोर करने में आप सहज नहीं हैं — देखें गोपनीयता।
कस्टम निर्देश और स्टाइल चैट्स के बीच मेमोरी रिट्रीवल-ऑगमेंटेड जेनरेशन (RAG) यह पेज साझा करें X LinkedIn Reddit Hacker News लिंक कॉपी करें

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-07-13। Reflect and the focus settings are in beta and evolving. Exact settings paths, plan availability, and what the recap surfaces can change — check Settings and the help center for current behavior. इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. What you'll learn Understand what Claude Reflect surfaces in your monthly recap — and what it doesn't See why it depends on memory being switched on Configure break reminders and quiet hours under Time and focus Weigh the genuine privacy trade-off before you turn it on Know how to read usage insights without letting them nudge you On July 9, 2026, Claude added two quietly personal features: Reflect (a monthly recap of how you use Claude) and Time and focus settings (break reminders and quiet hours). They're small in surface area but worth understanding, because they sit on top of your memory and shape how much of your usage Claude analyzes about you.

Reflect lives at Settings → Reflect. Once a month it surfaces: the topics you spent time on, your most active day and peak hour, and observations about how you work with Claude. It's in beta on Free, Pro, and Max, on the web and Claude Desktop. Watch out Reflect requires memory to be enabled. That's the key dependency: the recap is generated from what Claude retains about your conversations. No memory, no recap — and turning memory on to get the recap means Claude is also carrying facts about you across chats. Decide on the memory trade-off first; the recap is downstream of it.

Separately, Settings → Time and focus lets you configure optional break reminders and quiet hours to manage your own work patterns. These are nudges you opt into — a reminder to step away, and windows where Claude won't prompt you. Guided walkthrough1 of 4 1Turn on memory (if you want Reflect)⌄ Reflect is generated from memory, so enable it first — or skip Reflect entirely and use only Time and focus. ←PreviousNext→ 2Open Settings → Reflect⌄ On web or Claude Desktop, enable the monthly recap (beta). ←PreviousNext→ 3Read your first recap critically⌄ Treat topics, peak hour, and 'observations' as a mirror, not a scoreboard. ←PreviousNext→ 4Set Time and focus⌄ Under Settings → Time and focus, add break reminders and quiet hours that match how you actually want to work. ←PreviousNext→
documents.s: Time and focus: break reminders and quiet hours

documents.t: Usage-insight features are useful and also, by design, engagement-shaped: a recap that celebrates your "most active day" is a mirror, but it can also be a nudge to come back. Reporting on Reflect's launch framed it as quietly encouraging more AI use. That's not a reason to avoid it — it's a reason to read it deliberately. Pro tip A healthy way to use Reflect: skim the topics to notice where your attention actually went, ignore the streak-and-peak framing, and let quiet hours — not a recap — decide when you step away. The insight is the value; the gamification is optional.

Don't confuse the distinct things Claude calls "memory-adjacent": Feature What it does Needs memory on? Memory Carries facts about you across chats — (it is memory) Reflect Monthly recap of topics, peak time, work observations Yes Time and focus Break reminders and quiet hours No Projects Scoped context for a body of work No Check yourself 0/3 Key takeaways Reflect (Settings → Reflect) gives a monthly recap of topics, most active day, peak hour, and work observations — beta on Free, Pro, Max, web + Desktop. It requires memory to be enabled, because the recap is built from what Claude retains about you. Time and focus (break reminders, quiet hours) is separate and does not need memory. Usage recaps are engagement-shaped by design — read the topics as a mirror and let quiet hours, not streaks, govern your breaks.

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-06-20। वॉइस की उपलब्धता, समर्थित भाषाएँ और सटीक नियंत्रण ऐप और प्लान के अनुसार भिन्न होते हैं और अक्सर बदलते हैं — मौजूदा व्यवहार की पुष्टि आधिकारिक Claude हेल्प/डॉक्युमेंट में करें। इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. कभी-कभी सबसे तेज़ इनपुट आपकी आवाज़ होती है। वॉइस मोड आपको Claude से बात करने और इसके जवाब सुनने या पढ़ने देता है — विचार पकड़ने, ज़ोर से सोचने, या Claude का हैंड्स-फ़्री उपयोग करने के लिए बढ़िया।

चलते-फिरते विचार पकड़ना — एक अव्यवस्थित विचार बयान करें; Claude से इसे संरचित करने के लिए कहें। हैंड्स-फ़्री पल — चलना, आना-जाना, खाना बनाना। अभ्यास और विचार-मंथन — ज़ोर से एक आगे-पीछे का संवाद स्वाभाविक लगता है। सुगम्यता — कई लोगों के लिए बोलना टाइप करने से आसान हो सकता है (देखें सुगम्यता)।

Claude ऐप खोलें (आमतौर पर मोबाइल ऐप; उपलब्धता भिन्न होती है — ऊपर का नोट देखें)। चैट स्क्रीन से एक वॉइस बातचीत शुरू करें। स्वाभाविक रूप से बोलें; जब आप पूरा कर लें तो रुकें। Claude जवाब देता है, और एक ट्रांसक्रिप्ट चैट में सहेजा जाता है ताकि आप इसे दोबारा देख सकें या कॉपी कर सकें। आप आमतौर पर पुश-टू-टॉक और हैंड्स-फ़्री शैलियों के बीच स्विच कर सकते हैं, और यह बहुभाषी है — उस भाषा में बोलें जिसमें आप सोचते हैं।

माँग को सबसे आगे रखें। "मुझे एक शादी के भाषण की रूपरेखा बनाने में मदद करो — तीन मिनट, गर्मजोशी भरा और मज़ेदार" इधर-उधर भटकने से बेहतर काम करता है। जो फ़ॉर्मेट चाहते हैं उसे कहें। "मुझे पाँच बुलेट पॉइंट दो" — अन्यथा बोले गए जवाब भटक सकते हैं। ड्राफ़्ट के लिए इसका उपयोग करें, परिष्कृत करने के लिए स्क्रीन का। वॉइस से पकड़ें, फिर उसी चैट में टेक्स्ट को व्यवस्थित करें। वॉइस इन, टेक्स्ट आउट एक शक्तिशाली वर्कफ़्लो: वॉइस से ब्रेन-डंप करें, फिर टाइप करें "उसे एक साफ़ ईमेल में बदलो" — ट्रांसक्रिप्ट आपका कच्चा माल बन जाता है।

Markdown के रूप में कॉपी करें शुरुआती आखिरी बार सत्यापित: 2026-07-15। Screen reader mode, vimInsertModeRemaps, and fullscreen mouse-click support shipped in Claude Code v2.1.208 (July 14, 2026). Flag names, setting keys, and behavior can change between releases — confirm in the official changelog and settings docs. इसके विरुद्ध पुष्टि करें आधिकारिक स्रोत. Claude Code runs in the terminal — a text UI, which is a good starting point for accessibility, but the default rendering leans on color, box-drawing glyphs, and spinners that screen readers and some motor setups handle poorly. As of July 2026 there's a dedicated screen reader mode plus settings for vim ergonomics and mouse/scroll behavior. This page collects the levers that make the CLI usable with assistive tech. What you'll learn How to turn on screen reader mode — three ways, and what each changes What screen reader mode actually does to the transcript, tables, and permission prompts How to remap vim insert-mode keys (jj → Escape) to reduce hand strain How to control or disable mouse clicks and scroll acceleration in fullscreen Where high-contrast themes live, and how to report an accessibility gap

Screen reader mode swaps the decorative TUI for a plain-text rendering that assistive tech can read cleanly. Turn it on any of three ways — a one-off flag, an environment variable for every session, or a persistent setting. Guided walkthrough1 of 3 1Try it for one session⌄ Launch with the flag: claude --ax-screen-reader. Nothing else changes — same session, plainer output. ←PreviousNext→ 2Turn it on for every session⌄ Export the environment variable CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1 in your shell profile so it applies everywhere. ←PreviousNext→ 3Make it permanent in settings⌄ Set "axScreenReader": true in a settings.json file (user-level ~/.claude/settings.json applies to all projects). ←PreviousNext→ Persistent screen reader mode (~/.claude/settings.json) CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ { "axScreenReader": true }

Pro tip Plain-text rendering replaces the styled TUI so screen readers get clean, linear text. Decorative glyphs are hidden from screen readers instead of being read out as noise. Transcript symbols are announced as short labels rather than raw characters. Nested tables are read as Header: value. lines — flattened into speakable rows. Permission mode changes are announced aloud when you cycle modes with Shift+Tab. That last one matters: cycling permission modes with Shift+Tab is a core Claude Code interaction (see Permissions), and screen reader mode speaks the new mode aloud so you always know whether you're in plan, accept-edits, or auto mode without reading the status line.

If you use vim mode and reaching for Escape strains your hand, map a two-key insert-mode sequence to it instead. The vimInsertModeRemaps setting turns sequences like jj into Escape, so you never leave the home row. Map jj to Escape in vim mode (settings.json) CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ { "editorMode": "vim", "vimInsertModeRemaps": { "jj": "Escape" } } Watch out The remap only fires in insert mode, so typing jj as literal text needs a brief pause between keys — pick a sequence you rarely type fast (jj and kj are common choices). editorMode: vim enables vim keybindings; vimInsertModeRemaps only takes effect while vim mode is on.

Fullscreen menus now accept mouse clicks — including multi-select menus and the "Other" input rows — which helps if keyboard-only navigation is painful. Two settings tune pointer behavior for motion sensitivity or precision: Setting What it does CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS Disables mouse click, drag, and hover while keeping wheel scroll — useful if stray clicks disrupt you. wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled Set to false to turn off mouse-wheel scroll acceleration in fullscreen, for steadier, predictable scrolling. Steadier scrolling, no accidental clicks (settings.json) CopyCopied!Open in Claude↗ { "wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled": false, "env": { "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS": "1" } }

For low-vision users, terminal contrast is the first lever. Claude Code ships light and dark themes and supports custom themes you build from /theme or ship in a plugin — so you can dial in a high-contrast palette that meets your needs. See Settings for where theme choice is stored, and Output Styles if you also want plainer, less-decorated prose (the Explanatory and Learning styles are more verbose, not less — for terse output stay on Default). Beyond the CLI Screen reader mode covers the terminal. For hands-free interaction with Claude more broadly, Voice Mode in the app lets you talk and listen, and the Accessibility playbook covers using Claude itself as an assistive tool — simplifying text, building checklists, and adapting information to how you read. Check yourself 0/3 Pro tip Screen reader mode: --ax-screen-reader flag (once), CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1 (per shell), or axScreenReader: true (persistent). It plain-texts the transcript, hides decorative glyphs, flattens tables, and speaks permission-mode changes on Shift+Tab. vimInsertModeRemaps eases hand strain; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS and wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled tune pointer behavior. Custom themes give you high-contrast palettes; Voice Mode and the Accessibility playbook cover the rest.
